Elaine: Quick proposal — tighten gating on outbound log/SIEM exports and enforce short timebox + KMS-envelope keys for export payloads. Reason: limit blast radius from a compromised service account and make exports auditable. Sketch below, please review.

Samir: Can you call out the RBAC changes? who gets the new export role and how do we request it? :thinking:

Marta: @Samir +1. We also need an explicit audit trail for export requests that is stored outside the SIEM (immutable). Compliance will want a weekly review.

Isaac: For the connector side we can enforce an export TTL header and server-side reject if export_ttl expired. KMS integration: use data key envelope encryption, no long-lived decrypt grants. Prototype config snippet: 

```
export_policy:
  allowed_roles: ["sec_exporter", "sre_oncall"]
  export_ttl_secs: 172800  # 2 days
  kms_key_alias: "alias/redwood/siem-exports"
  require_approval: true
```

Ryan: For incident response, prefer ephemeral JIT access (Okta) + audit token and 2-approver emergency flow. Playbook idea: emergency_export -> two approvers -> 30m ephemeral access. Also we should emit structured audit events: `audit.event=export.request` with `requestor`, `approvers`, `reason`, `export_id`.

sec-bot: Alert: EXPORT_POLICY_CHANGE proposed by Elaine. Ticket created: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/SEC-3421

Elaine: RBAC plan: create a scoped role `siem_exporter` with `export:request` permission. Scope by project tags (so teams can only export their projects). Default: no principals. Requests via infra ticket for initial grant; ongoing access via JIT. Open to alternatives.

Samir: KMS question — do we grant decrypt to runtime or use envelope + ephemeral decrypt tokens? We should avoid any long-lived decrypt grants on compute nodes.

Marta: Envelope encryption + ephemeral decrypt tokens from KMS sounds right. Add retention and verification: exported objects must include metadata `x-redwood-audit-id` and be verified by Compliance weekly. If an export contains PII, auto-quarantine.

Isaac: Implementation note: runtime will call KMS.GenerateDataKey, use the plaintext locally to encrypt stream, then discard the plaintext key and store the encrypted data key with the object. We never persist plaintext data key. We'll also add `export_ttl` header so downstream consumers automatically purge after TTL.

Ryan: Suggest adding a canary export job that runs weekly to validate export permissions and policy drift detection. simple smoke tests + diff checks.

Elaine: Sounds good. I'll draft an RFC with these sections: RBAC model, KMS envelope flow, export TTL enforcement, audit schema, incident playbook. Meeting: 30-min sync tomorrow to finalize. Action items: @Samir draft RBAC rules, @Isaac prototype TTL header + KMS envelope, @Marta draft audit review cadence. :white_check_mark:

Marta: ack

Samir: will open PR with RBAC doc and link to RFC

Isaac: POC target EOD tomorrow, will post logs and sample S3 metadata `x-redwood-audit-id`
